etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From Middle English speciose, specious, from Anglo-Norman specious, Middle French specieux, and their etymon Latin speciōsus (“good-looking”).
senses: Seemingly well-reasoned, plausible or true, but actually fallacious.
Employing fallacious but deceptively plausible arguments; deceitful.

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
senses: Alternative form of speciose (“rich in species”).
